{{Short description|Von Neumann}}
In [[mathematics]], the notion of a '''cyclic and separating vector''' is important in the theory of [[von Neumann algebra]]s,<ref>{{Cite book|title=Les algèbres d'opérateurs dans l'espace hilbertien: algèbres de von Neumann|last=Dixmier|first=Jacques|author-link=Jacques Dixmier|publisher=Gauthier-Villars|year=1957|isbn=|location=|pages=}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite book|title=von Neumann algebras|last=Dixmier|first=Jacques|publisher=North-Holland|year=1981|isbn=|location=|pages=}}</ref> and, in particular, in [[Tomita–Takesaki theory]]. A related notion is that of a vector that is [[Cyclic vector|cyclic]] for a given operator. The existence of cyclic vectors is guaranteed by the [[Gelfand–Naimark–Segal construction|Gelfand–Naimark–Segal (GNS) construction]].

== Definitions ==
Given a [[Hilbert space]] ''H'' and a linear space ''A'' of [[bounded linear operator]]s in ''H'', an element Ω of ''H'' is said to be ''cyclic'' for ''A'' if the linear space ''A''Ω = {''a''Ω: ''a'' ∈ ''A''} is norm-dense in ''H''. The element Ω is said to be ''separating'' if ''a''Ω&nbsp;=&nbsp;0 for ''a'' in ''A'' implies that ''a''&nbsp;=&nbsp;0. Note that:

* Any element Ω of ''H'' defines a [[semi-norm]] ''p'' on ''A'', with ''p''(''a'') = ||''a''Ω||. The statement that "Ω is separating" is then equivalent to the statement that ''p'' is actually a [[Norm (mathematics)|norm]].
* If Ω is cyclic for ''A'', then it is separating for the commutant ''A′'' of ''A'' in ''B''(''H''), which is the [[von Neumann algebra]] consisting of all [[bounded operator]]s in ''H'' that commute with all elements of&nbsp;''A'', where ''A'' is a subset of ''B''(''H''). In particular, if ''a'' belongs to the commutant ''A′<nowiki/>'' and satisfies ''a''Ω&nbsp;=&nbsp;0 for some Ω, then for all ''b'' in ''A'', we have that 0&nbsp;=&nbsp;''ba''Ω&nbsp;=&nbsp;''ab''Ω. Because the subspace ''b''Ω for ''b'' in ''A'' is dense in the Hilbert space ''H'', this implies that ''a'' vanishes on a dense subspace of ''H''. By continuity, this implies that ''a'' vanishes everywhere. Hence, Ω is separating for ''A′''.

The following, stronger result holds if ''A'' is a [[*-algebra]] (an algebra that is closed under [[Hermitian adjoint|adjoints]]) and unital (i.e., contains the identity operator '''1'''). For a proof, see Proposition 5 of Part I, Chapter 1 of ''von Neumann algebras''.<ref name=":0" />

'''''Proposition''''' If ''A'' is a [[*-algebra]] of  [[bounded linear operator]]s on ''H'' and '''1''' belongs to ''A'', then Ω is cyclic for ''A'' if and only if it is separating for the commutant ''A′''.

A special case occurs when ''A'' is a [[von Neumann algebra]], in which case a vector Ω that is cyclic and separating for ''A'' is also cyclic and separating for the commutant ''A′''.

== Positive linear functionals ==
A [[positive linear functional]] ''ω'' on a [[*-algebra]] ''A'' is said to be ''faithful'' if, for any [[positive element]] ''a'' in ''A'', ''ω''(''a'')&nbsp;=&nbsp;0 implies that&nbsp;''a''&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.

Every element Ω of the Hilbert space ''H'' defines a [[positive linear functional]] ''ω''<sub>Ω</sub> on a  [[*-algebra]]  ''A'' of  [[bounded linear operator]]s on ''H'' via the inner product ''ω''<sub>Ω</sub>(''a'')&nbsp;=&nbsp;(''a''Ω,Ω), for all ''a'' in ''A''. If ''ω''<sub>Ω</sub> is defined in this way and ''A'' is a [[C*-algebra]], then ''ω''<sub>Ω</sub> is faithful if and only if the vector Ω is separating for ''A''. Note that a [[von Neumann algebra]] is a special case of a [[C*-algebra]].

'''''Proposition''''' Let ''φ'' and ''ψ'' be elements of ''H'' that are cyclic for ''A''. Assume that ''ω''<sub>''φ''</sub>&nbsp;=&nbsp;''ω''<sub>''ψ''</sub>. Then there exists an [[isometry]] ''U'' in the commutant ''A′'' such that&nbsp;''φ''&nbsp;=&nbsp;''Uψ''.
